newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Petkoff says salaries must rise.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Petkoff says salaries must rise.

text.p: One day before a national 12-hour work stoppage, Venezuela's Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff joined union calls for salary rises in the private sector.
"It's obvious that salary levels have to be adjusted now that the minimum wage has been raised. We all signed an agreement and the businessmen know they have to meet it," Petkoff told Union Radio.
Business, union and government leaders reached an agreement in March to reform Venezuela's severance payments and social security systems.
Under the agreement, the government raised the minimum wage by about 40 percent and private sector leaders pledged to raise salaries.
The Confederation of Venezuelan Workers (CTV), Venezuela's largest union, has called a 12-hour work stoppage for Wednesday to pressure for the wage rises.
Although the CTV draws most of its membership from public sector employees, oil sector, public transport and gas station workers will join the walkout.
Business chambers have said that 90 percent of their members have already raised salaries.
Petkoff said business leaders had "promised increases of 100 percent and then played the fool."
Government officials and political parties have generally supported the work stoppage, calling it a justified means of pressure.
Petkoff played down its impact and criticized those who talk about it "as if it were the end of the world."
